ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, building AD is 30m high. There is a distant tower BC. Someone at the bottom of the building A measures the elevation angle to the top of the tower to be $60^\circ$. After climbing to the top of the building D, the elevation angle to the top of the tower is measured to be $30^\circ$. What is the height of the tower BC in meters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the problem, we have: $BC=\frac{AC}{\tan 30^\circ}=\sqrt{3}AC$,\\
since $BE=DE\tan 30^\circ=AC\tan 30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}AC$,\\
therefore, the height of the building $AD=BC-BE=\left(\sqrt{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)AC=30$.\\
Thus, we find: $AC=15\sqrt{3}$.\\
Hence, $BC=\sqrt{3}AC=\boxed{45}$.

由 A 看 B 的仰角是 60°，所以直线 AB 的斜率满足 h/d=tan60°=√3，即 h=√3 d。
由 D 看 B 的仰角是 30°，所以直线 DB 的斜率满足 (h-30)/d=tan30°=1/√3。
把 d=h/√3 代入第二式：
(h-30)/(h/√3)=1/√3。
两边同乘 h/√3 得到 h-30=h/3。
因此 2h/3=30，解得 h=45。
所以塔 BC 的高度为 45 m。

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, building AD is 30 m high. There is a distant tower BC. Someone at the bottom of the building A measures the angle of elevation to the top of the tower to be $60^\circ$. After climbing to the top of the building D, the angle of elevation to the top of the tower is measured to be $30^\circ$. What is the height of the tower BC in meters?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: According to the problem, we have: $BC=\frac{AC}{\tan 30^\circ}=\sqrt{3}AC$, since $BE=DE\tan 30^\circ=AC\tan 30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}AC$, therefore the height of the building $AD=BC-BE=\left(\sqrt{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)AC=30$. Thus, $AC=15\sqrt{3}$. Hence, $BC=\sqrt{3}AC=\boxed{45}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: On the left side of the figure is building AD, A is at the bottom on the ground, and D is at the top of the building; on the right side is tower BC, C is at the bottom on the ground, and B is at the top of the tower. A and C are located on the same horizontal ground line. In the figure, from D to the right there is a horizontal dashed line to E on the tower body, so DE is parallel to AC and has equal length, and CE has the same height as AD. There are also dashed sight lines from A to B and from D to B, corresponding respectively to angles of elevation 60° and 30°.
Reasoning: Let AC = x. From right triangle ACB, tan 60° = BC / AC, so BC = x√3. From right triangle DEB, DE = AC = x, tan 30° = BE / DE, so BE = x / √3. Because CE = AD = 30, and BC = CE + BE, so BC - BE = 30. Substituting gives x√3 - x/√3 = 30, namely 2x/√3 = 30, solving gives x = 15√3. Therefore BC = x√3 = 15√3 × √3 = 45.
